newsitem.title: USA: North American Vaccine, Abbott in pact.
newsitem.headline: North American Vaccine, Abbott in pact.

text.p: North American Vaccine Inc and Abbott Laboratories Inc said on Tuesday they signed a definitive vaccine marketing and distribution agreement.
The agreement, preliminary terms of which were announced in August, calls for for a total investment of up to $42 million by Abbott, the companies said.
Under the pact, Abbott will market and distribute North American Vaccine's DTaP vaccine. The vaccine is against diphtheria, tetanus and acellular pertussis, or whooping cough.

In addition, Abbott will market and distribute North American Vaccine's combination vaccines currently under development that combine the DTaP vaccine with antigens for the prevention of polio and haemophilus influenza type b.
North American Vaccine submitted DTaP to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in September 1995 and final marketing approval is pending.

When approved, Abbott would market and distribute the DTaP vaccine and the combination vaccines to private physicians and managed care markets in the United States for immunization of infants and children, the companies said.
North American Vaccine will market the DTaP vaccine and the combination vaccines to government purchasers, including state governments and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
On signing the agreement, North American Vaccine received an equity investment, marketing fee and a clinical development payment totalling $13 million, the companies said.

Under the pact, North American Vaccine and Abbott will collaborate in the clinical development of the combination vaccines, and Abbott will provide North American Vaccine with clinical development funding, they said.
In addition North American Vaccine will receive payments when it reaches certain milestones. The first payment will be made upon FDA approval of the DTaP vaccine.
North American Vaccine will receive revenues from Abbott when Abbott buys the DTaP vaccine and the combination vaccine products for resale to the private pediatric market, the companies said.
